short: Highly successful Swedish Field Marshal who salvaged Sweden's military position after the disaster at Nördlingen.
full:
Johan Banér (1596–1641) was a brilliant, volatile, and famously hard-drinking Swedish Field Marshal who served under Gustavus Adolphus. Following the King's death at Lützen, Banér became one of the principal commanders of the Swedish forces in Germany. His leadership proved crucial during Sweden's darkest hours of the conflict.

Following the catastrophic defeat at Nördlingen in 1634, which nearly expelled Sweden from the war, Banér stabilized the situation. His stunning, against-the-odds victory at Wittstock in 1636 revived Swedish military prestige and forced the Imperial armies onto the defensive. He conducted a ruthless campaign of attrition until his death from illness in 1641, leaving the army in the capable hands of Torstensson.
